finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The file name 'fsm.dot' is hardcoded and not user-controlled. However, if the file name were user-controlled, this could lead to OS command injection.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any untrusted data source feeding the fopen call; the filename argument is a compile‑time constant string literal "fsm.dot" with no user or external input. No validation or sanitisation is required because the value cannot be altered at runtime. Consequently, no path exists from a tainted source to the fopen sink. No injection is possible.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.assumptions: The file name 'fsm.dot' is hardcoded and not user-controlled. However, if the file name were user-controlled, this could lead to improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the file name argument to fopen is a compile‑time string literal ('fsm.dot'), not an untrusted source such as argv, env var, or network data. Verified that there is no subsequent call that uses the file name in a system() or exec* invocation, so no OS command is constructed from the data. The sink is fopen, which merely opens a file, not an OS command executor. Therefore the CWE‑77 condition of improper neutralization of special elements in an OS command is not met.
